The **koordinerende netværksmøde** (coordinating network meeting) is a specific process within the Danish ADHD treatment pathway that was originally tracked by [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] in the ADHD Database [^src1]. The indicator was designed to measure whether a coordinating network meeting was held no later than 90 days after the start of a patient's ADHD assessment [^src1]. 

Throughout its entire lifespan, this specific metric consistently fell far short of its targets across regions and departments [^src1]. This chronic failure to meet the goals prompted a structural evaluation and strategic revision by the steering committee [^src1]. Recognizing that effective ADHD intervention requires early and structured collaboration between specialized psychiatry and the primary sector, the committee decided to retire the "koordinerende netværksmøde" metric [^src1]. It was substituted with a more operational, realistic, and cross-sectoral indicator focused on ensuring early contact with the patient's home municipality during the assessment phase [^src1]. 

This shift reflects a broader political and clinical acknowledgment that while cross-sectoral coordination is vital, the specific requirement of a formal network meeting within 90 days was not practically achievable, necessitating a more realistic metric for early municipal involvement [^src1].
